title: Santa Ana gale: the anchorage thins out, then refills
why: Gusts hit 36 kn on Nov 6-7. Part of the anchored fleet weighed anchor and rode it out under way; the queue fell from 10 to 6 ships. Once the wind dropped they came back: 12 ships on Nov 8.
model_note: 2024-11-07: model 9.3 vs persistence 6.2, actual 6.3 (persistence closer). Why: gusts reached 36 kn (ships that left anchor tend to return); pushes the forecast up. 2024-11-08: model 9.7 vs persistence 6.3, actual 12.0 (model closer). Why: gusts reached 36.3 kn (ships that left anchor tend to return); pushes the forecast up.

title: Storm swell halves the queue, and it bounces back
why: 3 m waves at the harbor-entrance buoy and 27 kn gusts on Nov 15-16. Anchored ships got under way inside the bay; the anchored count fell to 5.6. By Nov 18 it was back to 15.
model_note: 2024-11-16: model 9.4 vs persistence 7.1, actual 5.6 (persistence closer). Why: waves reached 2.9 m at the harbor entrance; pushes the forecast up. 2024-11-17: model 8.9 vs persistence 5.6, actual 9.4 (model closer). Why: gusts reached 27 kn (ships that left anchor tend to return); pushes the forecast up. 2024-11-18: model 11.2 vs persistence 9.4, actual 15.3 (model closer). Why: queue shrank by 4.8 ships over a week; pulls the forecast down.

title: December wind event: 18 -> 10 -> 15 ships
why: 32 kn gusts on Dec 10. Of the 20 ships anchored on Dec 9, five were drifting 20-30 nm offshore the next day, waiting it out at sea. The queue dropped to 10, then refilled to 14.5 on Dec 11. The model has no weather-forecast input, so it can't see a gale coming; what it learned is that the queue refills after one.
model_note: 2024-12-10: model 17.6 vs persistence 18.1, actual 10.1 (model closer). Why: gusts reached 9.9 kn; pulls the forecast down. 2024-12-11: model 12.3 vs persistence 10.1, actual 14.5 (model closer). Why: gusts reached 32.5 kn (ships that left anchor tend to return); pushes the forecast up.
